title: Let check-role-word skip machine-generated regions, not just directories
body:
Fixes #13586

Session: `https://claude.ai/code/session_01Pk26oZ12t5N1hwGW1m1MgC` (durable attribution copy, kept in prose because a body edit rewrites the footer).

## The gap, stated on the mechanism

`scripts/check-role-word.mjs` already holds the right position on machine-written content — the fix site for a generated occurrence is its **generator**, never the page. But it states that position as a directory **name**:

```js
const SKIP_DIRS = new Set(['node_modules', '.git', 'dist', 'references']);   // :57
if (SKIP_DIRS.has(e)) continue;                                             // :112
```

A name can only exempt a whole file. The repo's actual shape for derived content is finer: a machine-written **region inside a hand-written page**, delimited by a marker pair a generator writes and rewrites. Once such a region emits a source **path**, none of this gate's three remedies fit — rewording falsifies a path the generator re-emits on its next run, the vendor-wire fence admits declared upstreams only, and the baseline is maintainer-only and says so in as many words.

This is not just a reading of the gate. It is written down on `main` by a different author, in `scripts/tenant-audit-census.mjs`, as the reason that census put its rows in `docs/audits/` instead of on its own page:

> It also keeps 140-odd rows of machine output out of the published docs site, and out of `content/docs`-scoped prose ratchets that have no way to tell an emitted source path from an author's sentence -- `check-role-word` already excludes `content/docs/references/` for exactly that reason, and **a hybrid page is a shape its directory-level exclusion cannot express**.

That relocation is why the gate is green today. **Green is the workaround, not the gap closing.**

## The constructed demonstration, both directions

There is no live red on `main` to reproduce — the tripping row was moved out of both roots — so the case is **constructed**: a hand-written page carrying a generated region that emits `member-role-canonical.ts` (the hyphen is a word boundary, as the gate's own docblock notes).

**Direction 1 — the emitted path inside the region is exempt.** No baseline entry exists in the sandbox, so any counted occurrence would be a NEW use and exit 1; exit 0 is therefore exactly the claim "nothing was counted":

```
reserved-word occurrences in the file: 1
EXIT=0
check-role-word: OK, no new occurrences of the reserved word.
  Scanned: 1 .md/.mdx file(s) read across 2 root(s) — content/docs 1, skills 0.
  Exempt: 0 os:vendor-wire block(s) suppressed 0 occurrence(s); 1 generated region(s) suppressed 1 occurrence(s).
```

**Direction 2 — the SAME page, one author sentence added outside the region.** The ratchet is untouched:

```
reserved-word occurrences in the file: 2
EXIT=1
check-role-word: 1 problem(s)
  • content/docs/permissions/write-call-sites.mdx: NEW use of the reserved word "role" (1 occurrence(s)).
```

Two occurrences in the file, one counted. The identical fixture against the **unchanged** gate exits 1 on direction 1 as well — that is the defect, measured before the change.

## The shape

Skip the span from a `BEGIN GENERATED: REGION` marker to its matching `END GENERATED: REGION`, in whichever comment syntax the file's extension takes. The exemption stays greppable: a marker **pair in a diff**, never a property of a directory's name. The ratchet over author prose is untouched, and **no baseline entry moves** — the three live regions carry no occurrence today, so the ledger reads identically before and after.

## A malformed marker fails CLOSED

The direction-of-error question, answered first because it is the one that decides whether this is a ratchet or a suggestion. Every broken pair exempts **nothing** and is reported as its own class of problem, refusing before any verdict and **before `--update` can write**:

| broken pair | outcome |
| :--- | :--- |
| `BEGIN` with no matching `END` | exempts nothing, reported — honouring it would run the exemption to end of document, handing one line the whole rest of a page |
| `END` with no `BEGIN` open | exempts nothing, reported |
| `END` naming a **different** region | does not close the open one; both halves reported (pairing markers their authors did not pair is the fail-open direction) |
| a second `BEGIN` before the first closed | the first is reported unterminated, never nested silently |
| wrong comment syntax for the extension | delimits nothing, reported as an orphan |
| a marker naming no region at all | delimits nothing, reported as an orphan |

This is pinned at predicate **and** program level, and proven non-vacuous by ablations B and C below, which make it fail open and turn those legs red.

## The other three mechanism questions

**Marker discipline — reconciled, not duplicated.** The generated-region exemption reuses what the vendor-wire marker's stated rules are actually about: the `MARKER_SYNTAX` table (spelling keyed by **extension**), the fence scan (a marker shown inside a fence is example text, so the convention stays documentable in the roots it governs), the generous-detector / strict-claim split that turns an unrecognised attempt into a **loud orphan**, and the published volume on every run. The fence walk was extracted into one `scanFences()` so the two markers cannot disagree about where a fence ends.

Three rules it deliberately does **not** share, each a decision rather than an oversight:

- **The token is not this gate's to rename.** `VENDOR_WIRE_TOKEN` is spelled once because this gate invented it. `BEGIN GENERATED:` is a repo-wide convention owned by the generators that emit it; this gate is a consumer. It is still spelled once, so no diagnostic can point at a marker nothing recognises — but a rename would start at the generators.
- **No closed allowlist of region ids.** `VENDOR_BOUNDARIES` is closed because "whose vocabulary do we carry literally" is a policy decision with an ADR carve-out behind it. "Which generators exist" is not one; a list here would put a gate edit in front of every new census page, reinstating one layer down the maintainer bottleneck this card removes. Requiring the marker to name a generator path that **exists** was considered as a floor and rejected: any existing path would satisfy it, so it would check provenance in appearance only while coupling a vocabulary ratchet to file layout.
- **It is not offered as a remedy.** The refusal messages name the vendor-wire marker because an author may legitimately reach for it. This marker is a **fact about who wrote the text**, not a path an author may take; naming it in a refusal would read as an invitation to wrap prose in a marker pair and launder it. If a region is genuinely generated its occurrences were already skipped, so an author reading a refusal is by construction looking at their own prose.

**The span covers its own marker lines — decided, and pinned.** Both markers are emitted by the generator (`out.push(BEGIN_MARKER, …)` … `out.push(END_MARKER)`), so they are machine-written on the same footing as the rows between them, and the BEGIN line interpolates a generator **path** — exactly the string shape that trips this gate. Leaving it counted would make a region unshippable whenever its generator's own filename carries the word, and the only remedy left would be renaming the generator: the single-instance fix this exemption exists to replace. Pinned with a case whose positive control proves the marker really does carry the word.

**Three live instances, not two, and not spelled alike.** Beside `content/docs/ai/skills-reference.mdx:38` and `content/docs/permissions/tenant-audit-census.mdx:180` there is **`skills/README.md:28`**, inside the gate's second root, using the **HTML-comment** spelling rather than the MDX one. A parser built to a count of two would have been MDX-only and silently missed a whole root. All three carry a matching END, and the parser confirms it against the real corpus rather than against fixtures — the green line now reads `3 generated region(s)`.

A second measured asymmetry the count alone would have hidden: **BEGIN and END do not carry the same payload.** BEGIN is `REGION (generator path) — DO NOT EDIT`; END is the bare `REGION`. Matching on the whole payload would have paired nothing in the live corpus, so the region name is taken as the first word after the token.

## The self-test fails before the change and passes after

Extended in the gate's own `--self-test`, and each direction proven by ablation — mutation confirmed on disk by grep counts and a blob-hash comparison, restore proven by `git diff HEAD` emptiness against the HEAD blob, not by an exit code. (No build step is involved or claimed: this gate is a plain `.mjs` run directly by node, with no `dist/` in its resolution path.)

| ablation | named self-test failures |
| :--- | ---: |
| A — the span skip made inert (the pre-change behaviour) | 8, incl. both program-level legs |
| B — pair on any open region (fail-open on a name mismatch) | 1 |
| C — an unterminated BEGIN exempts to end of document (fail-open) | 4, incl. the `--update` byte-identity leg |

The in-process legs drive predicates; the program-level legs build real trees and read a child process's real exit status, so a predicate the program never consulted could not pass them. The two exemptions are proven **disjoint** against a fixture the vendor-wire scan *does* claim once the region mask is withheld — without that, a marked fence inside a generated region would be subtracted twice and drive a file's counted total negative.

## Why this is +687 / −37

Fair question for "skip a marked span". Measured composition of the 687 added lines:

| part | lines | share |
| :--- | ---: | ---: |
| self-test: the new pinned cases | 329 | 47.9% |
| parser + the six named refusal messages | 168 | 24.5% |
| design rationale docblock | 84 | 12.2% |
| shared `scanFences()` extraction + vendor-wire rewire | 34 | 4.9% |
| summary signatures + threading the new argument | 33 | 4.8% |
| published-volume clause | 25 | 3.6% |
| main scan loop wiring | 14 | 2.0% |

**Nearly half is the self-test the card asked for**, and 306 of 687 added lines (44.5%) are comments or docblocks — the house style of this file, which was already 1315 lines. The genuinely new production logic is the parser and its messages; the six refusal messages exist because fail-closed requires each broken pair to name itself rather than surface as a bare count.

The **one piece that was not strictly required** is the `scanFences()` extraction (34 added, most of the 37 deleted): the fence walk could have been duplicated instead. It is shared so the two marker conventions cannot disagree about where a fence ends — a divergence that would be invisible until a marker inside a fence was read as a claim. Flagging it explicitly so it can be judged as a deliberate refactor rather than found in review. Nothing else came along: one file changed, no unrelated fixes.

## Verification

All at `34e90e00b`, the final commit on this branch.

- `pnpm check:role-word` — green: self-test plus `Exempt: 0 os:vendor-wire block(s) suppressed 0 occurrence(s); 3 generated region(s) suppressed 0 occurrence(s)`, ledger unchanged at 43 files / 129 occurrences.
- **Gate family: 15 derived, 15 run**, `comm -23 derived ran` empty. 14 green; `check-test-completeness` exits **3 = PREREQUISITE NOT MET / NOT MEASURED** by its own definition (it grades a saved `turbo run test` log that only CI produces) — not a finding.
- `pnpm check:ratchet-remedy-authority` run **explicitly**, since it builds its scan surface at runtime and path derivation cannot name it: green, 180 scripts swept, 12 marked, 6 refusing. Doubly relevant here because this change adds refusal text to a gate that hands out remedies; the new messages offer no baseline-expanding path, so they take no authority marker, and the existing NEW-use message keeps its own.
- `pnpm lint` — the **full** repo scan, exit 0 in 1m56s. No narrowing claimed.
- `check-nul-bytes` green; the diff also scanned directly for raw control bytes.

The refusal **header** is now generic (`N marker problem(s)`), since two marker conventions report through one list and a header naming vendor wire over a generated-region defect would misdescribe it. Each message still names its own token, which is where that claim belonged.

## Changeset: none, deliberately

`scripts/` is repo tooling and publishes nothing, so there is no user-visible change. The precedent is unanimous — of the last 101 commits whose non-changeset files are all under `scripts/`, **101 carry no changeset**. `lint.yml` states the rule directly: "this PR edits a CI-internal script" is "the textbook `skip-changeset` case — such a PR releases nothing, so by the workflow's own prescription it takes the label."

**Record of who did what:** `Check Changeset` went red on this head while the PR carried only `size/l`. The **PM applied the `skip-changeset` label**, additively, after independently verifying that `scripts/` matches none of the `pnpm-workspace.yaml` package globs and that the root package is `private: true`. I did not write any label myself; I confirmed the resulting set (`size/l`, `skip-changeset`) by reading the PR back.
